gse_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Edge reasoning engine, the transferable value is threshold and trajectory reasoning: a persistence base rate of 15 percent, early-severity prognostic dominance, graded duration thresholds (PTA at 30 minutes and 4 hours), subsymptom-threshold dosing with ratchet-and-regress progression, an 80 percent derating of a measured tolerance boundary, an 85 percent efficiency controller for sleep scheduling, usage ceilings where a treatment flips into a cause, and masking-agent vetoes on clearance tests. These are reusable reasoning operators for any domain where the engine forecasts recovery, workload tolerance, or return-to-full-load timing, and they carry the guideline's own evidence grades as confidence weights.
gsi_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Institute, this is a model clinical-knowledge artifact: it shows how a mature field codifies definitions, severity indices, validated instruments (ACE, A-WPTAS, Rivermead, SCAT5, BCTT), decision rules such as the Canadian CT Head Rule, graded evidence, and consensus machinery (Delphi rounds, endorsement thresholds, prioritization votes) into one operational document. GSI can mine it for sports-medicine curriculum, for concussion protocol design in athletic settings, and as a worked example of converting heterogeneous evidence into auditable recommendations whose provenance and confidence are printed next to each claim.
motif_lane_note: Extracted under MOTIF-TIERB-DRAIN-01 by the Motif lane; quotes verified contiguous in the shipped extracted text.

assumptions: The injurious event is mechanical energy transfer to the head, neck or body, including indirect transmission to the brain
The definition is event-based and clinical; it does not require a positive imaging finding
primitives.breakdown_regime: The definition does not by itself grade severity and does not distinguish concussion from mTBI with intracranial injury; the guideline adds separate severity indices (GCS, PTA, LOC) and an imaging-based distinction for that. Penetrating injury is outside the guideline scope. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Supplies the engine's event definition for a head-impact exposure: an incident is registered when mechanical energy is transmitted to the brain, independent of whether downstream markers (imaging, symptoms) are positive. This separates exposure registration from outcome measurement, so severity and recovery models condition on a consistently defined event class.
layer2.telemetry: Mechanism-of-injury records (crash, fall, sport impact, assault), impact direction and site, and whether force was direct or transmitted through the body

primitives.name: Concussion/mTBI is the acute neurophysiological event related to blunt impact or other mechanical energy applied to the head, neck or body, with transmitting forces to the brain
primitives.page: Introduction, Definition of Concussion/mTBI (guideline p.1; text lines 273-276); repeated in Glossary (p.7)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Concussion/mTBI denotes the acute neurophysiological event related to blunt impact or other mechanical energy applied to the head, neck or body (with transmitting forces to the brain), such as from sudden acceleration, deceleration or rotational forces.

assumptions: Conventional neuroimaging (CT or standard MRI) is the reference test for the distinction
A persistent neurologic deficit is observable on clinical examination
primitives.breakdown_regime: The distinction collapses when only advanced imaging (DTI, fMRI) is abnormal, since the guideline treats those modalities as investigational for diagnosis; cases with normal conventional imaging remain classified as concussion even when symptoms are severe. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A subset relation with an evidence-triggered reclassification: the base class (concussion) is upgraded when a single hard marker fires. The engine can reuse this pattern wherever a soft-defined event is reclassified by one decisive observation rather than by accumulated score.
layer2.telemetry: CT and MRI reports, focal neurologic examination findings, and their timestamps relative to injury

primitives.name: All concussions are mTBI, but mTBI is distinguished from concussion when there is evidence of intracranial injury on conventional neuroimaging or a persistent neurologic deficit
primitives.page: Introduction (guideline p.1; text lines 267-270)
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is important to note that all concussions are considered to be a mTBI however mTBI is distinguished from concussion when there is evidence of intracranial injury on conventional neuroimaging or there is persistent neurologic deficit.

assumptions: GCS is typically measured at 30 minutes post-injury or on admission
Return of continuous memory can be established clinically or with a standardized PTA scale
primitives.breakdown_regime: The indices can disagree (a patient may score GCS 15 while still in PTA), and each is confounded by intoxication, sedation and pre-existing cognitive impairment; the guideline treats them as complementary rather than interchangeable, and notes mTBI can occur with no loss of consciousness at all. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Provides hard threshold features for severity stratification: three partially independent measurements (consciousness level, amnesia duration, LOC duration), each with an explicit mild-range cutoff. The engine can encode severity as a small vector of thresholded durations rather than a single opaque label, preserving which index drove the classification.
layer2.telemetry: Serial GCS scores, documented LOC duration, PTA duration from A-WPTAS or clinical assessment

primitives.name: Injury severity is indexed by GCS (mTBI = 13-15), loss of consciousness under 30 minutes, and post-traumatic amnesia, whose mild cutoff is usually placed at 24 hours or less
primitives.page: Introduction (guideline p.1; text lines 313-317)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Post-traumatic amnesia (PTA), measured as the time from when the trauma occurred until the patient regains continuous memory, is another criterion used to define injury severity, and the cut-off for mild injuries is usually placed at 24 hours or less.

assumptions: Imaging is performed with conventional clinical protocols
The statement concerns detection of structural abnormality, not exclusion of hemorrhage, for which CT remains the appropriate test
primitives.breakdown_regime: The limit applies to diagnosing concussion itself; CT retains a decisive role in excluding neurosurgically significant lesions such as hemorrhage, and advanced modalities such as DTI show group-level changes that are not consistent enough for individual diagnosis. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A negative-result asymmetry: absence of signal on the standard instrument carries almost no information about the condition, while a positive result is decisive. The engine should encode such instruments as one-sided evidence and never let a normal scan veto a clinically established event.
layer2.telemetry: Imaging modality, protocol, findings, and the clinical question the scan was ordered to answer

primitives.name: CT and conventional MRI usually fail to detect structural brain abnormality in mTBI, so normal imaging does not exclude the injury
primitives.page: Introduction (guideline p.1; text lines 297-299)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Computed Tomography (CT) and conventional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) usually fail to detect evidence of structural brain abnormalities in mTBI.

assumptions: Symptoms are assessed relative to the person's pre-injury baseline
The definition is duration-based and does not require proof that each symptom is caused by the brain injury itself
primitives.breakdown_regime: The symptoms are nonspecific and also occur in chronic pain, depression, PTSD and healthy populations, so the label describes a presentation rather than an etiology; the guideline handles this through mandatory differential diagnosis instead of tightening the definition. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Defines the engine's persistent-state class by duration and breadth across four symptom domains rather than by a single marker. A case enters the persistent class when multi-domain symptoms outlast the expected recovery window, which is the trigger for switching from acute management logic to symptom-by-symptom management logic.
layer2.telemetry: Serial symptom inventories across physical, cognitive, emotional and sleep domains, with onset and duration per symptom

primitives.name: Prolonged (persistent) symptoms are a variety of physical, cognitive, emotional and behavioural symptoms that may endure for weeks or months following a concussion
primitives.page: Introduction, Prolonged Symptoms (guideline p.2; text lines 340-343); Glossary (p.7)
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the purposes of this guideline prolonged symptoms refer to: A variety of physical, cognitive, emotional and behavioural symptoms that may endure for weeks or months following a concussion.

assumptions: The figure is a floor across studied populations, not a point estimate for any single cohort
The typical recovery frame referenced is 3 months
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rates vary widely by population and setting (the guideline cites 20 to 48 percent in veterans up to 60 months post-injury), and one cited longitudinal study found no recovery among patients whose post-concussion syndrome had lasted 3 years or longer, so the base rate must be re-based per population. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A prior probability for the persistent trajectory that any individual prognostic model must beat or update. The engine can carry 0.15 as the default prior for prolonged symptoms after concussion and update it with early symptom severity and risk-factor features instead of treating persistence as a surprise.
layer2.telemetry: Cohort-level persistence rates by setting (sport, motor vehicle, military, general emergency department), follow-up duration, and case-mix descriptors

primitives.name: Minimally 15 percent of persons with concussion experience persisting symptoms beyond the typical 3-month time frame
primitives.page: Introduction (guideline p.2; text lines 330-332)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Depending on the population studied the literature would suggest that minimally 15% of persons with concussion may experience persisting symptoms beyond the typical 3 month time frame.

assumptions: Phase is assigned by elapsed time since injury together with improvement trajectory
Post-acute non-improvement triggers referral to an interdisciplinary clinic; the persistent phase uses an individualized management approach focused on returning to pre-injury activities
primitives.breakdown_regime: Calendar phase alone misclassifies fast and slow recoverers; the guideline pairs the time bands with trajectory conditions (not improving, worsening), so phase transitions are partly state-based, and the framework is specific to adult mTBI care pathways. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A staged state machine for longitudinal management: the active intervention set, referral thresholds and monitoring cadence are functions of phase, and phase advances on both time and observed trajectory. The engine can reuse this as the control structure for any recovery or rehabilitation process it models.
layer2.telemetry: Days since injury, symptom trajectory slope between visits, referral events, and which phase-specific interventions were delivered

primitives.name: Treatment is phased by time since injury: acute (0-4 weeks) emphasizes education, reassurance, subsymptom threshold training and non-pharmacological interventions; post-acute (4-12 weeks) adds interdisciplinary referral; persistent (3 months and beyond) requires an interdisciplinary team
primitives.page: Introduction, Overall approach to treatment (guideline p.2; text lines 345-352)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Acute: (0-4 weeks): Emphasis should be placed on facilitation of recovery including education, reassurance, subsymptom threshold training and non-pharmacological interventions.

assumptions: Symptom domains interact, so improving a primary symptom such as sleep or depression can also improve secondary ones such as fatigue and cognition
Intervention availability and expected yield can be judged at the point of care
primitives.breakdown_regime: The hierarchy is a heuristic ordering, not a causal proof; a secondary symptom that blocks all participation, such as severe vertigo, may still need first attention in an individual case, and the guideline expects clinician judgment to override the default order. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A greedy sequencing rule for coupled problems: order interventions by tractability multiplied by expected cross-domain spillover, because the domains are causally coupled. The engine can reuse this as a general policy for sequencing fixes in any interacting system rather than attacking the loudest or hardest component first.
layer2.telemetry: Per-domain symptom severity, intervention availability, and measured cross-domain change after each targeted treatment

primitives.name: Treatments are prioritized hierarchically: first target symptoms that have readily available interventions and the potential to yield significant symptomatic and functional improvement (depression, anxiety, sleep, headache) before secondary symptoms (balance, dizziness, cognition, fatigue, tinnitus)
primitives.page: Scope and Purpose, Directives for Use (guideline p.6; text lines 548-551); Table B, Symptom Treatment Hierarchy
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is recommended that treatment be first targeted at specific difficulties that have both readily available interventions and the potential to yield significant symptomatic and functional improvement.

assumptions: Grades were harmonized across source guidelines by re-grading each recommendation against this single scheme
Grade expresses strength of supporting evidence, not size of clinical effect
primitives.breakdown_regime: Most prolonged-symptom recommendations rest on grade C because high-quality trials are scarce in that area; the grade measures evidence maturity, and a C grade does not mean a recommendation is unimportant, since several C recommendations are implementation priorities. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A provenance weight attached to every rule the engine emits: each recommendation travels with the class of evidence behind it, so downstream reasoning can discount or flag conclusions that rest only on consensus. The engine can adopt the same three-tier tagging for any ingested claim set.
layer2.telemetry: Evidence type per recommendation, source guideline or study, and the grade assigned at harmonization

primitives.name: Every recommendation carries an evidence grade: A means at least one randomized controlled trial, meta-analysis or systematic review; B means at least one cohort comparison, case study or other experimental study; C means expert opinion, experience or consensus panel
primitives.page: Unique Features and Symbols (guideline p.III; text lines 236-240); Methodology, Table D (p.74)
primitives.verbatim_quote: LEVEL A: At least one randomized controlled trial, meta-analysis or systematic review

assumptions: The patient is an adult with minor head injury in the rule's validated population
CT is available; where it is not, the guideline's algorithm directs consideration of transfer
primitives.breakdown_regime: The rule triages imaging need; it does not diagnose concussion and does not clear a patient from follow-up, since symptoms can evolve and delayed complications are handled through observation criteria and discharge advice. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A validated decision rule gating an expensive, decisive test: imaging is ordered only when pre-test risk features cross the rule threshold. The engine can reuse this shape for any costly diagnostic: enumerate the risk features, fix the threshold by external validation, and let the rule, not intuition, fire the test.
layer2.telemetry: GCS at 2 hours, vomiting, age, suspected skull fracture, seizure, coagulopathy, mechanism of injury, and CT result

primitives.name: The need for early neuroimaging after mTBI is determined by the Canadian CT Head Rule; when criteria are met, CT is the appropriate investigation to exclude neurosurgically significant lesions such as hemorrhage, and plain skull x-rays are not recommended
primitives.page: Key Recommendations, Recommendation 1.3 (guideline p.8; text lines 650-653); Section 1 (p.14)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The need for early neuroimaging should be determined according to the Canadian CT Head Rule (Figure 1.1).

assumptions: Symptoms are formally documented at the initial assessment so later comparison is possible
The predictor is early total symptom burden, not any single symptom
primitives.breakdown_regime: Prediction is probabilistic and population-level; individual recovery still varies with the risk factors in Table 1.1 and with later complications, and the claim rests on the cited prognostic literature rather than on a score derived inside this guideline. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: An early-measurement dominance result: the earliest dense measurement of the outcome variable itself outpredicts elaborate baseline features. For engine prognostics this argues for instrumenting the first days heavily and using early trajectory as the primary recovery feature, with static risk factors as modifiers.
layer2.telemetry: Standardized symptom scores at presentation and over the first days, plus Table 1.1 risk-factor flags for adjustment

primitives.name: The severity of a person's symptoms in the initial few days after TBI is the strongest and most consistent predictor of slower recovery, and demonstrates clinical utility in tracking recovery
primitives.page: Section 1 narrative (guideline p.12; text lines 935-938)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The severity of a person's symptoms in the initial few days after a TBI is the strongest and most consistent predictor of slower recovery, and demonstrates clinical utility in tracking recovery.

assumptions: PTA is objectively tested, for example with the A-WPTAS, rather than estimated from patient report alone
The thresholds operate inside the algorithm's wider low-risk versus high-risk feature set
primitives.breakdown_regime: PTA duration is one factor among many in the algorithm; the presence of multiple risk factors is explicitly more concerning than a single isolated factor, and intoxication or poor motivation can distort PTA measurement. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A two-threshold duration rule that converts a continuous measurement into graded risk bands (minor versus major). The engine can reuse graded duration thresholds wherever exposure time itself is the risk carrier, instead of forcing binary cutoffs.
layer2.telemetry: Objective PTA duration in minutes, A-WPTAS scores over time, and co-occurring algorithm risk factors

primitives.name: In the initial diagnosis algorithm, PTA over 30 minutes is a minor risk factor and PTA over 4 hours a major risk factor for intracranial injury
primitives.page: Algorithm 1.1, explanatory notes (guideline p.17; text lines 1243-1245)
primitives.verbatim_quote: PTA > 30 mins is a minor risk factor and PTA > 4 hours a major risk factor for intracranial injury.

assumptions: The memory component takes less than a minute to administer and is repeated hourly alongside a standardized GCS assessment
The total score combines GCS (out of 15) with the A-WPTAS memory component for a total of 18
primitives.breakdown_regime: It is a screening device, not a full cognitive assessment; poor motivation, depression, pre-morbid intellectual handicap and medication, drug or alcohol effects can distort scores, and the guideline instructs clinical judgment where doubt exists. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A minimal repeated probe that converts an unobservable state (being in PTA) into a scored time series with a crisp exit threshold (18/18). The engine can reuse this pattern: short standardized probes, fixed cadence, and a predeclared exit score for state tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Hourly A-WPTAS total and memory-component scores, GCS, and time to first 18/18

primitives.name: The Abbreviated Westmead PTA Scale (A-WPTAS) is a screening tool for promptly assessing cognitive problems such as memory loss or amnesia directly following concussion/mTBI; it is administered hourly with the GCS and a score of 18/18 marks emergence from PTA
primitives.page: Methodology, Resource Evaluation example (guideline p.72; text lines 4697-4699); Appendix 1.2 (pp.80-82)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The A-WPTAS was developed as a screening tool for promptly assessing any cognitive problems, such as memory loss or amnesia directly following concussion/mTBI.

assumptions: A validated scale is used consistently, such as the Rivermead Post Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire or the Post Concussion Symptom Scale
The comparison baseline is the patient's pre-injury state
primitives.breakdown_regime: Self-report scales inherit reporting biases and symptom nonspecificity; scores track burden and change rather than proving injury causation, and some patients under-report because they are not fully aware of their symptoms or their functional impact. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Longitudinal comparability is manufactured by fixing the instrument: the same scale, the same anchors, every visit, until resolution. The engine should treat instrument identity as part of the datum, because change scores are only meaningful within one instrument's frame.
layer2.telemetry: Scale name and version, per-item and total scores per visit, days since injury at each administration

primitives.name: Somatic, cognitive/communication and emotional/behaviour symptoms after mTBI should be documented using a standardized assessment scale at the initial appointment and at follow-up appointments until symptoms resolve
primitives.page: Section 1, Recommendation 1.8 (guideline p.15; text lines 1118-1120)
primitives.verbatim_quote: be documented using a standardized assessment scale (see Appendices 1.5 and 1.6) at the

assumptions: Education covers symptoms, the expected course of recovery, and gradual return to activities and life roles
Delivery is early, verbal, and backed by written patient information sheets, with follow-up sessions over the initial 12 weeks as required
primitives.breakdown_regime: Effects are preventive and probabilistic, shown for early educational interventions; education does not treat established severe symptoms, and content must be tailored to the patient's history and symptoms rather than delivered generically. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: An expectation-setting intervention with a measurable outcome effect: calibrating the subject's model of the process (what is normal, what recovery looks like) changes the trajectory itself. The engine can treat expectation calibration as an active intervention variable in any human-in-the-loop forecast, not as neutral information transfer.
layer2.telemetry: Timing and content of education delivered, written materials provided, follow-up contact schedule over the first 12 weeks

primitives.name: Reassurance in addition to education about symptoms is more effective for lowering the risk of prolonged symptoms than education alone, and brief single-session education-oriented treatment is superior to standard procedures
primitives.page: Section 2 narrative (guideline p.19; text lines 1375-1377)
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is also evidence to suggest that reassurance, in addition to education about symptoms, is more effective for lowering risk of prolonged symptoms than education alone.

assumptions: The claim concerns complete rest as a prescription, not the brief 24-48 hour relative rest the guideline still allows
The evidence judgment follows the 5th International Conference on Concussion in Sport consensus statement
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient evidence is not proof of harm for every patient; a short period of rest in the acute symptomatic period may still benefit individuals, and the guideline's positive recommendation is graded activity, a separate claim with its own support. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A null-evidence flag on a traditional default: when the inherited default intervention has no supporting evidence, the engine should mark it unproven rather than treating tradition as a prior. This is the guideline's mechanism for retiring legacy rules without needing proof of harm.
layer2.telemetry: Rest prescriptions issued, their duration, and symptom course under rest versus graded activity

primitives.name: There is currently insufficient evidence that prescribing complete rest eases discomfort during acute recovery or promotes recovery by minimizing brain energy demands following concussion
primitives.page: Section 3, Recommendation 3.4 (guideline p.25; text lines 1788-1792); Key Recommendations (p.9)
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is currently insufficient evidence that prescribing complete rest may ease discomfort during the acute recovery period by mitigating post-concussion symptoms and/or that rest may promote recovery by minimizing brain energy demands following concussion.

assumptions: Activity is titrated against symptom response, not pushed through exacerbation
Vigorous exertion and activities with concussion risk remain excluded during recovery
primitives.breakdown_regime: The threshold is individual and shifts during recovery, so no fixed activity prescription can implement the rule; patients who worsen need re-assessment for treatable drivers (cervical, vestibular, mood, sleep) rather than simple activity reduction. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A feedback-controlled dosing rule: the dose (activity) increases progressively but is capped by a measured response variable (symptom exacerbation), making the patient's own threshold the controller. The engine can reuse threshold-capped escalation for any rehabilitation or exposure process it schedules.
layer2.telemetry: Activity type and duration per day, symptom change during and after activity, estimated individual exacerbation threshold over time

primitives.name: After a brief period of rest during the acute phase (24-48 hours), patients should be encouraged to become gradually and progressively more active while not increasing symptoms, staying below their cognitive and physical symptom-exacerbation thresholds
primitives.page: Section 3 narrative (guideline p.22; text lines 1619-1621); Recommendations 4.5 and 5.5
primitives.verbatim_quote: Therefore, after a brief period of rest during the acute phase (24-48 hours) after injury, patients should be encouraged to become gradually and progressively more active while not increasing symptoms.

assumptions: The statement concerns complete rest, distinct from relative rest and from sleep
It applies to the typical mTBI course managed in primary care
primitives.breakdown_regime: The guideline states this as emerging evidence with a 'may'; it does not license forcing activity on patients with red-flag features, unstable injuries or severe acute symptoms, who follow the assessment and observation pathway instead. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: An inactivity penalty with a time constant: beyond roughly two to three days, the default do-nothing branch turns negative. The engine can encode rest as an intervention with a decaying benefit curve that crosses zero, rather than as a neutral baseline.
layer2.telemetry: Hours of complete rest prescribed and actually taken, day of first graded activity, recovery milestones

primitives.name: Complete rest exceeding 48 to 72 hours may slow recovery
primitives.page: Section 5 narrative (guideline p.29; text lines 2022-2024)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore there is evidence that complete rest exceeding 48 to 72 hours may slow recovery.

assumptions: Specialized interdisciplinary services exist and are accessible
Risk factors from Table 1.1 can justify earlier referral than the 1-month mark
primitives.breakdown_regime: Referral timing is a capacity and triage rule, not a biological threshold; where clinics are unavailable the guideline substitutes an interdisciplinary formal network of providers, and primary care management continues in the interim. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: An escalation ladder keyed to persistence: an unresolved state at checkpoint one buys specialist assessment, and at checkpoint two buys team treatment. The engine can reuse fixed checkpoints with escalating resource commitment for any stalled process it supervises.
layer2.telemetry: Symptom status at 1 and 3 months, referral dates, clinic type, wait times

primitives.name: Persons with prolonged symptoms at 1 month post-injury may be indicated for referral to specialized interdisciplinary assessment, and patients with prolonged symptoms at 3 months post-injury should be referred for interdisciplinary treatment if available
primitives.page: Section 4 narrative (guideline p.27; text lines 1883-1885)
primitives.verbatim_quote: For persons with prolonged symptoms at 1 month post-injury, referral for specialized assessment in an interdisciplinary concussion clinic may be indicated.

assumptions: Interactions are clinically documented pairings, such as sleep disturbance with mood, pain, cognition and fatigue
Treating a driver symptom is expected to relieve coupled symptoms
primitives.breakdown_regime: The guideline asserts interaction qualitatively without a quantitative interaction model; clinicians must infer the local coupling structure per patient, and misidentifying the driver symptom wastes the treatment sequence. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Symptoms form a coupled network, not independent channels: the state of one node is an input to others. The engine should model symptom domains as a graph with directed exacerbation edges and evaluate interventions by their downstream node effects, which is exactly what the treatment hierarchy exploits.
layer2.telemetry: Co-occurrence and lagged correlation of domain scores across visits, and response of untreated domains to a targeted treatment

primitives.name: Post-concussive symptoms interact: the assessment and management of prolonged symptoms should be directed toward specific symptoms while considering etiology, elapsed time, and the fact that some symptoms exacerbate others
primitives.page: Section 4, Recommendation 4.2 (guideline p.27; text lines 1905-1909)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Primary care providers should be aware of symptom interaction as

assumptions: Recognition can be performed by any sport stakeholder; formal diagnosis is made by a physician after thorough medical assessment
Suspicion, not confirmed diagnosis, is the removal trigger
primitives.breakdown_regime: Removal is a safety rule whose cost is false positives; it does not apply to non-sport settings in the same form, and the guideline notes that sport-specific guidance may not transfer directly to other injury types. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A suspicion-triggered stop rule with asymmetric error costs: when the cost of a missed event dwarfs the cost of a false alarm, the trigger is suspicion rather than confirmation. The engine can reuse this asymmetry explicitly wherever it sets alert thresholds on high-harm events.
layer2.telemetry: Sideline recognition events, removal decisions, assessment outcomes, same-day return violations

primitives.name: Any player suspected of having a sport-related concussion should be immediately removed from play, must not return to the game or practice, and should be referred for medical assessment
primitives.page: Section 3 narrative (guideline p.22; text lines 1607-1610)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Experts unanimously agree that any player suspected of having experienced a concussion/mTBI should be immediately removed from play, must not return to the game or practice and should be referred for Medical Assessment.

assumptions: Progression starts only after an initial 24-48 hours of relative physical and cognitive rest
Each step is gated on being asymptomatic at the current level, and full-contact practice requires medical clearance
primitives.breakdown_regime: The ladder is calibrated for sport; symptoms prolonged beyond 10-14 days in adults or 1 month in children exit the ladder into specialist management, and resistance training is withheld until stage 3 or 4 at the earliest. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A ratchet protocol with regression: advance one stage per time quantum while the state is clean, drop exactly one stage on violation, never skip. The engine can reuse this staged ratchet for any return-to-full-load process where overshoot is costly and detectable.
layer2.telemetry: Stage reached per day, symptom response per stage, regressions, time to full clearance

primitives.name: Return to sport follows a graduated six-stage strategy (symptom-limited activity, light aerobic exercise, sport-specific exercise, non-contact training, full-contact practice, return to sport) with at least 24 hours per step; if symptoms worsen during exercise, the athlete goes back to the previous step
primitives.page: Section 3, Table 3.2 notes (guideline p.24; text lines 1732-1735); Recommendation 3.8
primitives.verbatim_quote: There should be at least 24 hours (or longer) for each step of the progression. If any symptoms worsen during exercise, the athlete should go back to the previous step.

assumptions: Symptom status is the clearance signal, so anything that alters the signal invalidates the test
The decision to return while still on medication must be considered carefully by the primary care provider
primitives.breakdown_regime: The rule protects the measurement rather than the pharmacology itself; medications needed for comorbid conditions create genuine trade-offs that the guideline leaves to individualized interdisciplinary judgment, including retirement decisions after multiple concussions. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A measurement-integrity veto: a clearance test is invalid while any agent that can suppress the measured signal is active. The engine should encode masking agents as test invalidators in any domain where clearance is granted on a symptom or signal readout.
layer2.telemetry: Medication list with start and stop dates relative to clearance date, symptom scores on and off medication

primitives.name: Return-to-play requires the athlete to be free from concussion-related symptoms and also not taking any pharmacological agents or medications that may mask or modify the symptoms of sport-related concussion
primitives.page: Section 3, Recommendation 3.9 (guideline p.25; text lines 1818-1822)
primitives.verbatim_quote: an important consideration in return-to-sport is that concussed athletes should not only be free from concussion-related symptoms, but also should not be taking any pharmacological agents/medications that may mask or modify the symptoms of SRC.

assumptions: The test is a graded treadmill protocol recording heart rate, RPE and symptom severity each minute, terminated on significant exacerbation (an increase of more than 3 points on the Likert scale from resting score) or maximal exertion
The BCTT is not recommended for patients scoring higher than 7/10 for symptom severity, and cervical, vestibular and cardiac contraindications are screened first
primitives.breakdown_regime: The 80 percent figure is a protocol constant from the BCTT manual, not a fitted optimum; patients who exercise to voluntary exhaustion without symptoms are routed to return-to-play staging instead, and patients with symptoms but no physiologic threshold are redirected to cervical, vestibular or temporomandibular evaluation. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: Threshold measurement converted directly into a safe operating dose: find the failure boundary under controlled load, then set the working point at a fixed fraction (0.8) of it. The engine can reuse boundary-then-derate prescription wherever a system's tolerance can be probed safely.
layer2.telemetry: Heart rate at symptom exacerbation, RPE and Likert scores per minute, prescribed target heart rate, adherence and symptom response to the prescription

primitives.name: On completion of the Buffalo Concussion Treadmill Test, concussion patients may be given an exercise prescription based on 80 percent of the maximum heart rate reached without symptom exacerbation, exercised at that level for 20 minutes daily
primitives.page: Appendix 3.3, BCTT Instruction Manual, Outcomes (guideline p.114; text lines 7610-7612)
primitives.verbatim_quote: On completion of the BCTT, concussion patients may be given an exercise prescription based on 80% of the maximum heart rate reached without symptom exacerbation.

assumptions: The patient can learn to recognize their significant symptom threshold, the boundary of the red danger zone
A symptom increase of 2-3/10 that returns to baseline within 30-60 minutes is treated as an appropriate dose signal, and timers are used to stop tasks soon after symptom onset
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pacing is a patient-education tool from one hospital outpatient ABI team and its graphs are schematic; the approach presumes symptoms are a usable gauge, which fails when patients cannot perceive or report symptom change reliably. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A two-sided error model for dosing: under-dosing and over-dosing are both failure modes, and the correct dose is found by feedback against a personal threshold. The engine can encode activity prescriptions as a control problem with an interior optimum rather than a monotonic more-is-better rule.
layer2.telemetry: Planned versus completed activity bouts, timer use, symptom excursions and time to return to baseline, crash episodes requiring hours or days of recovery

primitives.name: Activity pacing: doing nothing at all will not promote recovery, but doing too much each day may cause prolonged symptoms, so structured paced activity below the significant symptom threshold, with planned rest breaks, is ideal
primitives.page: Appendix 2.2, The Parkwood Pacing Graphs (guideline p.100; text lines 6440-6446)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Doing nothing at all will not promote recovery, but doing too much each day may cause prolonged symptoms.

assumptions: Post-traumatic headache is a secondary headache subtype whose treatment pathway follows the primary category (migraine-like or tension-type) its clinical characteristics best fit, per ICHD-III criteria
Comorbid conditions such as PTSD are assessed because they contribute to the complexity of management
primitives.breakdown_regime: The 30-90 percent range is too wide for individual prediction and reflects heterogeneous study populations; the guideline notes some post-traumatic headaches are currently unclassifiable, so the phenotype scheme carries an explicit residue class, and post-traumatic headache should not be treated as an isolated condition. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A wide base-rate band plus phenotype routing: prevalence is carried as an interval, and treatment selection is delegated to a sub-classifier (migraine-like versus tension-type). The engine can mirror this by keeping interval-valued priors and routing cases to phenotype-specific playbooks instead of one generic pathway.
layer2.telemetry: The focused headache history of Table 6.1 (frequency, duration, location, intensity, quality, associated symptoms, provoking and alleviating factors), headache-related disability days, phenotype assignment

primitives.name: Anywhere from 30-90 percent of individuals who sustain an mTBI develop post-traumatic headache; it is more common after concussion/mTBI than after severe TBI, and is classified and treated by the primary headache phenotype it most closely resembles
primitives.page: Section 6 narrative (guideline p.33; text lines 2243-2245)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Studies to date have documented that anywhere from 30-90% of individuals who sustain a mTBI develop post-traumatic headache.

assumptions: Use frequency is counted in days per month and tracked with a headache diary and medication calendar
Suspected overuse is tested by withdrawing the offending medication for a washout period of at least 6-8 weeks
primitives.breakdown_regime: The ceilings are class-level rules from headache medicine applied to post-traumatic headache largely by expert consensus; individual susceptibility varies, and the guideline notes it can be very challenging to distinguish headache severity from medication overuse as the perpetuating cause without the washout test. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A treatment that becomes a cause past a usage threshold: the same variable is therapy below the ceiling and pathology above it. The engine should model such interventions with a sign flip at a counted threshold (days per month) and count exposure explicitly rather than assuming monotonic benefit.
layer2.telemetry: Medication class, days used per month, headache days per month, diary completeness, washout outcomes

primitives.name: Acute headache medications carry monthly ceilings to avoid medication-overuse (rebound) headache: less than 15 days per month for simple analgesics, and no more than 10 days per month for combination analgesics, narcotic analgesics, ergotamines, triptans and diclofenac potassium oral solution
primitives.page: Section 6 narrative (guideline p.33; text lines 2267-2271); Recommendation 6.8 (p.34)
primitives.verbatim_quote: combination analgesics, narcotic analgesics, ergotamines, triptans, and diclofenac potassium oral solution can be utilized no more than 10 days per month to avoid medication overuse (rebound) headache.

assumptions: Prevalence is by patient report; subjective complaints and objective polysomnography findings can disagree, though objective alterations have been measured in acute and chronic stages
Insomnia is the most common form in the subacute and chronic stages, while the acute stage may show an increased need for sleep
primitives.breakdown_regime: Sleep disturbance is frequently secondary to depression, anxiety, PTSD or pain, so prevalence does not establish the injury as the cause in an individual case; less common disorders such as sleep-related breathing disorder, restless legs and REM sleep behaviour disorder require specialist evaluation and polysomnography. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A high-prevalence, multi-form disturbance class that sits upstream of mood, cognition, communication and occupational outcomes, and is itself a prognostic factor for functional and social outcomes up to one year. For the engine this makes sleep a hub variable: measure it early and in all cases, because its state conditions the interpretation of several other domains.
layer2.telemetry: Sleep interview and questionnaire results (Appendices 7.2 and 7.3), sleep diary metrics, polysomnography where indicated

primitives.name: More than 50 percent of patients report sleep disturbances following mTBI, spanning insomnia, hypersomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, poor sleep maintenance, poor sleep efficiency, early awakening, delayed sleep onset and alterations in circadian cycle
primitives.page: Section 7 narrative (guideline p.38; text lines 2560-2563)
primitives.verbatim_quote: More than 50% of patients report sleep disturbances following mTBI, specifically insomnia, hypersomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, poor sleep maintenance, poor sleep efficiency, early awakening, delayed sleep onset, or alterations in circadian cycle.

assumptions: CBT-I targets the factors perpetuating insomnia: unhealthy sleep hygiene, maladaptive sleep habits, autonomic and cognitive arousal, and dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes about sleep

Where formal CBT-I is unavailable or awaited, primary care providers can implement behavioural recommendations (restriction of time in bed and stimulus control) with weekly monitoring for the first few weeks
primitives.breakdown_regime: The recommendation is grade B and rests substantially on the general insomnia literature; melatonin evidence after mTBI is mixed, and sleep medications carry dependency and adverse-cognition cautions in this population, which is why the behavioural route holds first place. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A mechanism-targeted behavioural protocol outranks symptom-suppressing drugs when the disorder is maintained by learned and behavioural factors. The engine can encode treatment selection as mechanism matching: identify the maintaining mechanism class first, then pick the intervention class that acts on it.
layer2.telemetry: CBT-I referral and completion, sleep diary trends, hypnotic prescriptions and their durations

primitives.name: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia is established as the treatment of choice for either primary insomnia or insomnia comorbid to a medical or psychiatric condition
primitives.page: Section 7, Recommendation 7.7 (guideline p.39; text lines 2663-2665)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for insomnia is established as the treatment of choice for

assumptions: Sleep is monitored with a sleep diary for 1-2 weeks before the window is set
The window is maintained for at least one week before adjustment, with a consistent wake time even on weekends, under healthcare professional supervision
primitives.breakdown_regime: The rule presumes accurate diary data and a patient who can tolerate transiently increased sleepiness in the first days or weeks; the guideline attaches an explicit caution for driving and operating machinery during titration. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A proportional controller with a setpoint: measure efficiency (sleep divided by time in bed), compare it against the 85 percent threshold, and adjust the controlled variable (window length) in fixed 15-20 minute increments on a weekly cycle. The engine can lift this controller wholesale for any efficiency-titrated schedule.
layer2.telemetry: Diary-derived total sleep time, time in bed, sleep efficiency percentage, window adjustments, daytime sleepiness ratings

primitives.name: Sleep restriction titration: set the sleep window to actual sleep time (not less than 5.5 hours) with fixed bedtime and rising time; if the patient sleeps more than 85 percent of time spent in bed, increase the window by 15-20 minutes weekly, and if less than 85 percent, decrease it by 15-20 minutes
primitives.page: Appendix 7.5, Behavioural Recommendations for Optimal Sleep (guideline p.134; text lines 8680-8686)
primitives.verbatim_quote: If you sleep more than 85% of time you spend in bed and/or you constantly feel sleepy during the day, increase the sleep window by 15-20 minutes.

assumptions: Mental health is assessed within the individual's biopsychosocial context, including pre-existing history and losses of role, income and independence
Etiology may be reactive (the trauma experience, lost work or school roles), neurobiological, or driven by chronic symptoms such as pain and poor sleep
primitives.breakdown_regime: The cycle is a qualitative systems claim, not a parameterized model; the guideline also states there is no current evidence that post-mTBI mental health problems should be treated differently from mental health problems of other etiologies, so the cycle guides breadth of assessment rather than novel therapy. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A positive feedback loop between a hub state (mood) and the symptom domains, which makes single-domain treatment plans systematically underpowered. The engine should detect loop structure and prefer interventions that break the loop at its highest-gain edge, consistent with the guideline's treat-sleep-and-mood-first hierarchy.
layer2.telemetry: PHQ-9, GAD-7, PC-PTSD-5 and PCL-5 scores, pain and sleep scores, and functional status, tracked jointly over time

primitives.name: Mental health disorders are major determinants of post-mTBI wellness and functional recovery, and form a vicious cycle of pathology in which disorders of mood exacerbate chronic pain, sleep disturbance, anergia and cognitive inefficiencies, which feed back into the mood disorder
primitives.page: Section 8 narrative (guideline p.43; text lines 2775-2778)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Reciprocally, in what can be considered a 'vicious cycle of pathology', disorders of mood can exacerbate chronic pain, sleep disturbance, anergia and cognitive inefficiencies.

assumptions: The concussion/mTBI population may be more sensitive to adverse medication effects on cognition (alertness, attention, memory), balance and dizziness, sleep and fatigue, and headaches, so agents are screened against those domains
Successful pharmacotherapy is continued for at least 6 months before a trial of slow tapering, and maintenance treatment after successful antidepressant treatment is advised for at least 6-9 months
primitives.breakdown_regime: Much supporting evidence is extrapolated from non-TBI populations, which the guideline states explicitly for PTSD agents; benzodiazepines are excluded from first-line use because they do not reduce the core symptoms of PTSD and carry arousal, cognition, motor coordination and dependency risks. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: First-line selection by collateral-damage profile rather than by raw efficacy: among effective agents, prefer the class whose side effects least disturb the already-compromised domains. The engine can reuse side-effect-aware ranking whenever it recommends interventions into a fragile system.
layer2.telemetry: Agent and dose trajectory, target symptoms monitored, adverse effects on arousal, cognition, sleep and motor coordination, response at regular follow-up intervals

primitives.name: SSRIs and SNRIs are recommended as first-line pharmacotherapy for diagnosed mental health conditions following concussion/mTBI, based on side-effect profile and broader utility compared with other classes; prescribing starts at the lowest effective dose, titrates slowly, and changes one medication at a time
primitives.page: Section 8 narrative (guideline p.46; text lines 3030-3034); Recommendations 8.6-8.7 and Table 8.1
primitives.verbatim_quote: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and Serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) are recommended as first-line treatments for diagnosed mental health conditions following concussion/mTBI, based upon their side-effect profile and broader utility when compared to agents from other classes.

assumptions: BPPV attacks typically last less than 30 seconds and are provoked by sudden position change such as rolling over in bed or looking up
The Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre is performed once the cervical spine has been cleared
primitives.breakdown_regime: Repositioning is specific to BPPV; other dizziness causes (post-concussion migraine, autonomic dysregulation, central vestibular dysfunction, medication effects) need different management, and the cited Cochrane evidence finds repositioning more effective than vestibular rehabilitation for BPPV specifically, while vestibular rehabilitation is the recommended treatment for unilateral peripheral vestibular dysfunction. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A mechanical fault with a mechanical fix, gated by a provocative diagnostic test: confirm the displaced-particle hypothesis with Dix-Hallpike, then physically reverse the displacement. The engine can reuse test-then-reverse structure wherever a reversible physical displacement is the candidate mechanism.
layer2.telemetry: Dix-Hallpike result by side, vertigo episode duration and triggers, Dizziness Handicap Inventory score, response to repositioning

primitives.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, caused by dislodged otoconia in the posterior semicircular canal, is the most common cause of post-traumatic peripheral vestibular dysfunction; a canalith repositioning (Epley) manoeuvre should be used to treat it if the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre is positive
primitives.page: Section 10, Recommendation 10.3 (guideline p.54; text lines 3495-3498); Section 10 narrative (p.53)
primitives.verbatim_quote: A canalith repositioning maneuver should be used to treat benign positional vertigo (BPPV) if the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre is positive.

assumptions: Fatigue is multidimensional (physical, cognitive, motivational, psychological) and is assessed by focused history plus a scale such as the Barrow Neurological Institute Fatigue Scale

Secondary causes (affective disorder, sleep disorder, metabolic causes including hypothyroidism and anemia, electrolyte abnormality, polypharmacy) are screened before fatigue is attributed to the injury
primitives.breakdown_regime: The 27.8 percent figure comes from the cited systematic review literature and varies by cohort; fatigue perception can be out of proportion to exertion or occur without exertion, and the guideline reports no significant relationship between pituitary growth hormone deficiency and post-mTBI fatigue despite earlier suggestions. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A state variable with hysteresis: presence at the 3-month checkpoint raises the probability of presence at 6 months, so the checkpoint measurement carries prognostic information beyond current burden. The engine can treat checkpoint persistence as a distinct feature from point prevalence in any chronic-symptom model.
layer2.telemetry: BNI Fatigue Scale or Fatigue Severity Scale scores, fatigue dimensions (physical versus mental), medication review flags, status at 3 and 6 months

primitives.name: Fatigue is one of the most pervasive symptoms following concussion/mTBI, with 27.8 percent of individuals experiencing persistent fatigue at 3 months post-injury; those with fatigue at three months are increasingly likely to continue experiencing it beyond six months
primitives.page: Section 11 narrative (guideline p.56; text lines 3605-3608)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fatigue is one of the most pervasive symptoms following concussion/mTBI, with 27.8% of individuals experiencing persistent fatigue at 3 months post-injury.

assumptions: Restrictions, limitations and abilities are communicated to the employer and other stakeholders, with appropriate consents, to facilitate temporary accommodations
The existence of symptoms at baseline is not, in itself, a basis for no return to work; what matters is whether work tasks exacerbate symptoms
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tolerance cannot be certified medically, so plans built only on clinician judgment misprice it; in complex or safety-sensitive cases where restrictions and limitations cannot be clearly defined, the guideline calls for an interdisciplinary vocational evaluation. no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: A three-way decomposition of a return-to-load decision into hazard (risk), capability (capacity), and subjective endurance (tolerance), each owned by a different assessor. The engine can reuse this decomposition for any graded return protocol and should refuse to collapse the three into a single readiness score.
layer2.telemetry: Documented restrictions, limitations and symptom triggers, job demands, accommodations offered, progression of hours and duties

primitives.name: Work readiness after concussion/mTBI is assessed by defining risk (medical restrictions), capacity (limitations), and tolerance (the ability to tolerate symptoms, which is not a medically answerable question), then formulating a progressive return-to-work plan that keeps the worker below symptom-exacerbation threshold levels
primitives.page: Section 12 narrative (guideline p.60; text lines 3905-3908); Table 12.2 stepwise approach
primitives.verbatim_quote: An accepted and effective approach to assess work readiness is for the healthcare provider to define "risk" (medical restrictions), "capacity" (limitations), and "tolerance"

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The guideline is full of vetoes that override local optimization. A normal CT cannot veto a clinical diagnosis of concussion. Suspicion of concussion vetoes continued play on the day of injury. Any medication that masks symptoms vetoes return-to-play clearance. Symptom exacerbation vetoes progression to the next return-to-sport stage and forces a one-stage regression. Medication-overuse ceilings veto continued acute headache prescribing. Red-flag signs veto discharge and sideline handling in favour of emergency assessment. Finally, the evidence grade vetoes false confidence: grade C recommendations, which carry most of the prolonged-symptom content, must not be presented with grade A certainty.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The guideline descends from the Ontario Neurotrauma Foundation guideline program begun in 2008, through first and second editions, updated here by the Graham and Harrison Guidelines Adaptation Cycle. Its recommendations are adapted from the Motor Accidents Authority NSW guideline of 2008, the VA/DoD concussion guidelines of 2009 and 2016, SIGN guidance, and the Concussion in Sport Group consensus statements, Zurich 2012 replaced by Berlin 2016. Its instruments are inherited artifacts: the ACE from Gioia and Collins and the CDC Heads Up toolkit, the A-WPTAS from Shores and Lammel at Westmead, the Rivermead questionnaire from King and colleagues in 1995, SCAT5 from the Concussion in Sport Group in 2017, the BCTT from the Buffalo concussion program, and headache criteria from the ICHD-III beta of 2013.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The authors write for a busy primary care clinician who is the hub of care but not the whole team. They assume this reader needs recommendations that stand alone by section, carry explicit evidence grades, and convert directly into visits, referrals and patient handouts. Their model of the patient is a person whose symptoms are real but nonspecific, whose expectations about recovery are themselves therapeutic, and whose main dangers are deterioration missed early, recovery stalled by over-rest, and symptoms treated in isolation while their drivers go unaddressed. They assume a coordinating clinician plus an interdisciplinary network can be mobilized when simple care fails, and that standardized instruments make individual clinicians reliable.
reasoning_traces.think: This guideline is a clinical operating system for one problem: an adult sustains a mild traumatic brain injury, most recover within days to three months, and a minority, at least 15 percent, do not. Everything in the document is organized around separating those two trajectories early and managing the second one symptom by symptom. It opens by fixing the event definition. Concussion and mTBI name the same acute neurophysiological event, mechanical energy transmitted to the brain, and the pair is pried apart only when conventional imaging shows intracranial injury or a persistent neurologic deficit appears. Severity is then indexed with three partly independent rulers, Glasgow Coma Scale 13 to 15, post-traumatic amnesia at or under 24 hours, and loss of consciousness under 30 minutes, with the explicit warning that mTBI can occur with no loss of consciousness at all. Because CT and conventional MRI usually show nothing in mTBI, diagnostic weight falls on history, examination and standardized symptom documentation, while imaging is reserved for a validated triage rule, the Canadian CT Head Rule, whose job is to exclude surgical lesions rather than to confirm concussion. The acute front end has its own machinery. Algorithm 1.1 sorts patients by risk features, observation runs at least four hours with deterioration defined by alertness, behaviour, cognition, PTA, vomiting or severe headache, and discharge is gated on normal mental status plus written and verbal advice cards, with a named follow-up clinician. The A-WPTAS turns post-traumatic amnesia into an hourly scored measurement with an 18 out of 18 exit. Small rules carry the same signature: a symptomatic patient must not drive for at least 24 hours, and a compensation claim must not be read as secondary gain. The management core is a phased state machine. In the acute phase, zero to four weeks, the work is education, reassurance and subsymptom-threshold activity. In the post-acute phase, four to twelve weeks, non-improvement triggers interdisciplinary referral. Beyond three months the patient belongs to an interdisciplinary team with an individualized plan. Inside that machine sit several strong, transferable claims. Early symptom severity is the best predictor of slow recovery, so the first measurement matters most and must be taken with a fixed instrument, the Rivermead questionnaire or the Post Concussion Symptom Scale, repeated until resolution. Complete rest is demoted: the evidence for it is insufficient, rest beyond 48 to 72 hours may slow recovery, and the replacement is graded activity dosed against the individual's symptom-exacerbation threshold, a controller that reappears as pacing graphs for daily life, as the six-stage graduated return-to-sport ladder with 24-hour steps and one-stage regression on symptom recurrence, and as the Buffalo Concussion Treadmill Test, which measures the heart rate at exacerbation and prescribes exercise at 80 percent of it. Symptoms are treated as a coupled network rather than a list. The treatment hierarchy attacks first the domains with ready interventions and large spillover, depression, anxiety, sleep and headache, because mood and sleep disorders demonstrably worsen pain, fatigue and cognition, in what the mental health section calls a vicious cycle of pathology. Each domain chapter then supplies its own operators. Headache is phenotyped against ICHD-III categories and fenced by medication-overuse ceilings, under 15 days a month for simple analgesics and 10 days for triptans and combination agents, with a 6 to 8 week washout as the diagnostic test for overuse. Sleep is handled with CBT-I as the treatment of choice and a quantitative sleep-restriction controller that titrates the sleep window against an 85 percent efficiency setpoint in 15 to 20 minute weekly steps. Mental health care borrows general-population algorithms wholesale, with SSRIs and SNRIs first line, one medication change at a time, and explicit screening of side effects against already compromised domains. Vestibular care shows the opposite pattern, a specific mechanical fault, BPPV from dislodged otoconia, with a provocative test, Dix-Hallpike, and a physical reversal, the Epley manoeuvre. Return to work is decomposed into risk, capacity and tolerance, with tolerance explicitly marked as not medically answerable. Other chapters fill in the same pattern. Cognitive symptoms that persist past four weeks earn a neuropsychological referral rather than more reassurance. Vestibular care splits by mechanism: repositioning beats rehabilitation for BPPV, while rehabilitation is the answer for unilateral peripheral dysfunction, and vestibular suppressant medication is explicitly not supported. Fatigue is treated as multidimensional and screened for secondary causes from sleep apnea to polypharmacy, with a warning that stimulants can buy a burst of energy at the price of deeper fatigue afterward. The guideline also issues confident negative rules where the evidence warrants them, most sharply a grade A recommendation against hyperbaric oxygen. The document is also honest about its own construction. Recommendations were adapted from earlier guidelines and a systematic review that screened 52,687 records down to 82 included studies, graded A, B or C, filtered through modified Delphi rounds with an 80 percent agreement rule, retained on level A evidence or at least 75 percent endorsement, and prioritized by expert votes into key recommendations. The prolonged-symptom half of the guideline rests mostly on grade C consensus, and the authors say so. Where the work breaks is where any consensus guideline breaks: thresholds like 15 percent, 27.8 percent, 80 percent and 85 percent are borrowed from heterogeneous studies and single protocols, symptom reports are nonspecific and overlap with depression, chronic pain and PTSD, and several recommendations repeat across sections because each chapter was written to stand alone. Its durable value is not any single number but the reasoning pattern: define the event, measure early with fixed instruments, phase the response, dose against thresholds, cap what becomes harmful, and escalate on schedule when the state does not resolve.

universal_lens: This guideline is a template for managing any complex, multi-domain, mostly self-limiting condition with a persistent minority. Define the event crisply. Instrument it with standardized repeated measures from the first encounter. Publish the base rate of the bad trajectory. Phase the response by time and by observed trajectory. Sequence treatments by tractability and cross-domain spillover rather than by loudness. Dose activity against a measured personal threshold, with a ratchet that advances on success and regresses one step on violation. Cap interventions that become causes past a counted ceiling. Escalate to a team at fixed checkpoints when the state fails to resolve, and grade the evidence behind every rule so users know which rules are measurements and which are consensus.
